newsitem.title: GERMANY: Grundig CEO van der Wal steps down.
newsitem.headline: Grundig CEO van der Wal steps down.

text.p: Grundig AG chief Pieter van der Wal will resign as chief executive of the troubled German electronics maker, the IG Metall union said on Monday after a supervisory board meeting.

IG Metall said after a crisis meeting of Grundig's supervisory board that van der Wal would step down. Several hundred workers demonstrated outside management offices against van der Wal, who had called for job cuts to restore Grundig to profitability.
Van der Wal will leave Grundig within two months, IG Metall said. The supervisory board also agreed that no Grundig units would be sold during that time.

The union, which had also sought the resignation of supervisory board chief Christian Schwarz-Schilling, gave no further information on the board's plans. But a management news conference was scheduled for Monday afternoon.

Van der Wal's turnaround plan called for laying off 2,000 of Grundig's 8,500 workers this year after a 250 million mark loss in 1996. He had also announced plans to sell a video and security systems business and shift TV production out of Germany to Austria.

Van der Wal was hired less than a year ago by Dutch giant Philips Electronics NV, which gave up control of the company on January 1, ending a costly effort to revive one of Germany's best known brand names.
